The objectives of this notebook will be to conduct exploratory data analyses on site inherent characteristics of the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet Clean version using the baseline conditions (HA 10% Closed System). This file should be run after the EDA.Rmd

# Preparing the Variables

Set the working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt_sep/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis")
```

Upload the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

dat <- read_excel("Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

# Preview
head(dat)
```

## 1. Sites Within Networks

```{r}
library(dplyr)

sites_by_network <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Network, Site) %>%
  distinct() %>%                     # remove duplicates
  group_by(Network) %>%
  summarise(
    Sites = paste(Site, collapse = ", "),
    n_Sites = n()
  )

sites_by_network
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Name excel sheet
# -------------------------------------------------------
file_path <- "Inherent_characteristics_summary.xlsx"

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load if exists, otherwise create new workbook
# -------------------------------------------------------
if (file.exists(file_path)) {
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)
} else {
  wb <- createWorkbook()
}

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create sheet if it does NOT exist
# -------------------------------------------------------
if (!"Sites by Network" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Sites by Network")
}

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Add data to the tab (overwrites ONLY that sheet)
# -------------------------------------------------------
writeData(wb, sheet = "Sites by Network", sites_by_network)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Save workbook without erasing other sheets
# -------------------------------------------------------
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

```

## 2. Inherent Characteristics

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# variables to summarize
cat_vars <- c(
  "Development",
  "Distance_from_EFPC",
  "Drainage_area",
  "Relative_elevation",
  "Orientation",
  "Regime"
)

rel_freq_table <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(cat_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Value) %>%
  summarise(Freq = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  mutate(RelFreq = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

rel_freq_table
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Name excel sheet
# -------------------------------------------------------
file_path <- "Inherent_characteristics_summary.xlsx"
```

Correlation of metrics indicative of stream size/order/position within the watershed

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Select variables
vars_to_select <- c("Relative_elevation_m", "Dist_from_EFPC_km", "Drainage_area_km2")

scaled_vars <- as.data.frame(
  scale(dat[vars_to_select])
)

library(corrplot)

# Create correlation matrix from DATA, not names
cor_matrix <- cor(
  scaled_vars,
  method = "pearson"
)

# Plot
corrplot(
  cor_matrix, 
  method = "color",
  type = "lower",
  tl.cex = 0.7,
  tl.col = "black",
  addCoef.col = "black",
  number.cex = 0.6
)
```

Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) of inherent characteristics

```{r}
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(dplyr)

cat_vars <- c(
  "Development",
  "Distance_from_EFPC",
  "Drainage_area",
  "Relative_elevation",
  "Orientation",
  "Regime"
)

cat_data <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(cat_vars)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

mca_result <- MCA(cat_data, graph = FALSE)

# ------------------------------
# Results
# ------------------------------
# 1. Eigenvalues: shows the most important dimensions explaining most of the variance
eig_df <- as.data.frame(mca_result$eig) %>%
  mutate(
    Dimension = paste0("Dim ", seq_len(n()))
  ) %>%
  select(
    Dimension,
    eigenvalue = eigenvalue,
    percent_variance = `percentage of variance`,
    cumulative_percent = `cumulative percentage of variance`
  )

# 2. Contributions of the categories on each dimension
# Rule-of-thumb threshold
contrib_threshold <- 100 / nrow(mca_result$var$contrib)

# Convert contributions to tidy table
contrib_df <- mca_result$var$contrib %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    Category = rownames(.)
  ) %>%
  relocate(Category)

# View
eig_df
contrib_df
```

Save results

```{r}
file_path <- "Inherent_characteristics_summary.xlsx"

# ------------------------------
# Load or create workbook
# ------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  wb <- createWorkbook()
} else {
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)
}

# ------------------------------
# Helper: add or overwrite sheet
# ------------------------------
add_or_replace_sheet <- function(wb, sheet_name, data) {
  if (sheet_name %in% names(wb)) {
    removeWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
  }
  addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
  writeData(wb, sheet_name, data)
}

# ------------------------------
# Write MCA results
# ------------------------------
add_or_replace_sheet(wb, "MCA_Eigenvalues", eig_df)
add_or_replace_sheet(wb, "MCA_Category_Contributions", contrib_df)

# Optional: threshold metadata (nice for transparency)
add_or_replace_sheet(
  wb,
  "MCA_Notes",
  data.frame(
    Item = c("Contribution threshold (%)"),
    Value = contrib_threshold
  )
)

# ------------------------------
# Save
# ------------------------------
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

Plot and save

```{r}
mca_plot <- fviz_mca_var(
  mca_result,
  repel = TRUE,
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  label = "var",     # only show variable names
  title = "MCA Variable Vectors"
)

# View
mca_plot

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = "MCA_variable_vectors.png",
  plot = mca_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

```
